items.stem: An industrial hygienist compares a full-shift noise dose to an occupational exposure limit. Which quantity is most appropriate for assessing continuous and intermittent noise over the shift?

options.text: Time-weighted average (TWA) sound level over the sampling period
options.rationale: Correct: a TWA integrates varying levels over time and is compared to a full-shift limit.

options.text: The single highest instantaneous peak reading
options.rationale: Peak readings assess impulsive-noise limits, not full-shift average exposure.

options.text: The arithmetic mean of three spot readings
options.rationale: A few spot readings do not represent time-weighted exposure across a varying shift.

options.text: The manufacturer's rated level for the loudest machine
options.rationale: Equipment ratings are not a measurement of the worker's actual exposure.

items.explanation: Correct: a TWA integrates varying levels over time and is compared to a full-shift limit.

items.stem: When selecting controls for a solvent-vapor exposure, which option reflects the preferred engineering control over administrative measures?

options.text: Installing local exhaust ventilation at the point of vapor generation
options.rationale: Correct: local exhaust ventilation is an engineering control that captures the contaminant at the source.

options.text: Rotating workers to limit each person's exposure time
options.rationale: Job rotation is an administrative control that distributes rather than reduces the hazard.

options.text: Requiring respirators for all exposed workers
options.rationale: Respirators are PPE, used when engineering controls are insufficient.

options.text: Posting the safety data sheet near the work area
options.rationale: Providing information is administrative and does not reduce airborne concentration.

items.explanation: Correct: local exhaust ventilation is an engineering control that captures the contaminant at the source.

items.stem: Select TWO factors that most directly affect a chemical's inhalation hazard in a workplace.

options.text: The airborne concentration of the substance in the breathing zone
options.rationale: Correct: breathing-zone concentration is a primary determinant of inhalation dose.

options.text: The vapor pressure (volatility) of the substance
options.rationale: Correct: higher volatility increases the tendency to generate airborne vapor.

options.text: The color of the container the chemical is stored in
options.rationale: Container color has no bearing on inhalation hazard.

options.text: The alphabetical order of the chemical's name
options.rationale: Naming has no effect on the physical hazard.
Supplier brand does not determine the inhalation hazard of the substance itself.

items.explanation: Correct: breathing-zone concentration is a primary determinant of inhalation dose.
